solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beg mischief-maker to take on new role

indicators.note: a new version of something is a remade one, so the letters come out in a fresh order

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous little sprite
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a troublemaker to accept a fresh part to play.
explanation.walkthrough: IMP takes on a reworked ROLE, which becomes LORE, to give IMPLORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore someone is to plead with them earnestly, a straightforward synonym for asking humbly.

clue.text: Popular youngster primarily interpreting nightmares

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A well-liked child is chiefly good at explaining bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular youngster' reads as one idea, a well-liked child, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi (plural of incubus) are demons thought to lie on sleepers, and by extension oppressive nightmares.

clue.text: Maybe one astride a heavy carthorse?

blocks.note: whimsically, a rider astride something is one who perches on it
a breed of powerful draught horse from the Perche region of France

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PERCHER ON: one who perches on, which is what a rider astride does. The question mark flags the invented phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Percheron is a French breed of big draught horse, originally bred in the Perche area of Normandy.

clue.text: Old friend in Paris collecting gear for pastime in Japan

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
ami is French for friend
a rig is a set of equipment or outfit

explanation.surface: An elderly French pal picks up kit for a hobby practised in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: O and AMI together take in RIG: O-AMI collecting RIG gives O(RIG)AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami, the art of folding paper into figures, is a traditional Japanese craft and hobby.

clue.text: Mournful English supporter going over Iowa and California

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a leg supports a table or a body
IA is the US postal code for Iowa
Cal is a common short form for California

explanation.surface: A sad English fan travels over two American states.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going over' just means placed above, so the English supporter sits on top of the two state abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiacal is a rarer form of elegiac, describing the sorrowful tone of an elegy or lament.

clue.text: Attend police station, not having caught one-time dropout

indicators.note: not having something means going without it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to attend is to be at, split as BE AT
nick is British slang for a police station
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone shows up at the police station without having been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: BE AT + NICK with its C taken out. 'Caught' looks like arrest, but it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks of the 1950s rejected conventional society, so the term describes a past-era countercultural dropout.

clue.text: Member of cattle tribe thus invading waste container perhaps

indicators.note: an invader goes inside territory, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: a bin is one example of a waste container
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A cow-like beast barges into a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the fragment as just one example of a waste container, not the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bison belong to the bovine tribe Bovini alongside domestic oxen and buffalo, making them members of the cattle family.

clue.text: Memory defect mother raised upset first-class nurse once

indicators.note: in a down clue raising something lifts it so it reads bottom to top
to upset is to tip over, so the letters are turned end to end

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a former British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A forgetful condition afflicts a mother, who was raised by an old-school top nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: MA turned up gives AM; A1 plus SEN turned over gives NESIA. SEN was a British nursing qualification, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, whether partial or total, caused by injury, illness or shock.

clue.text: New girl meets head of Roedean? I don’t believe it!

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Eve is a girl's name
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A new pupil is introduced to the headmistress of a posh girls' school, to general astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: N + EVE + R. Roedean is a famous English girls' boarding school, which is why 'head' sounds like its headmistress.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'Never!' expresses shocked disbelief, exactly like saying you can't credit something.

clue.text: Scene of cat fights? Type disturbing a fellow

indicators.note: something disturbing breaks into the middle of things, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: Kenny is a man's name, standing for any chap
ilk means type or kind

explanation.surface: Where do cats scrap? Some sort of creature is bothering a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kilkenny cats of the old rhyme fought until only their tails were left; 'a fellow' stands for any man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish town gives its name to the legendary Kilkenny cats, who fought each other to mutual destruction.

clue.text: State of hair in dogs outside bars?

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: curs are mongrel dogs
bars and lines are both straight marks or stripes

explanation.surface: Dogs tied up outside pubs, and the condition of their coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs, and 'dogs outside bars' a scene outside one, but bars here are just straight lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Curliness describes how curly something is, a condition hair has when it forms ringlets or waves.

clue.text: Month the Spanish produce literary work

blocks.note: Nov is the calendar abbreviation for November
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: In one particular month, Spaniards turn out a book.
explanation.walkthrough: NOV + EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a book-length prose fiction, the most familiar kind of literary composition.

clue.text: Chap inside stole tea

indicators.note: being inside something means enclosed by it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur
a chap is a he

explanation.surface: A man indoors pinched some tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb meaning pinched, but it is the noun: a scarf worn round the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea was a black China tea, widely drunk in eighteenth-century Britain and America.

clue.text: Irish island where drinks are on the house?

definitions.text: where drinks are on the house?

blocks.note: a small island in Lough Gill, County Sligo, made famous by Yeats

blocks.clueFragment: where drinks are on the house?
blocks.note: whimsically, a pub where everything is gratis: the pub is free

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as INN IS FREE: a pub that charges nothing. The question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake Isle of Innisfree, subject of W B Yeats's poem, is a real island in an Irish lough.

clue.text: Control plant’s rebirth

blocks.note: to rein in is to control
a carnation is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: Managing a plant so that it springs back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: REIN + CARNATION; the apostrophe-s stands for 'is' linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is the soul being born again in a new body, a literal second birth.

clue.text: Bring back army corps court covering most of county

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
Surrey is an English county south of London
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A military unit and a law court are restored across much of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + SURRE(Y) + CT. Surrey is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurrect is to revive something dead or disused, returning it to life or use.

clue.text: Artisan travelling north is crossing motorway

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move, so these letters shift into another order
to cross something is to go across its middle, so one piece lies inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A craftsman heading north crosses a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling north' looks like an instruction to read upwards, but 'north' is plain letters for rearranging. The M1 is Britain's main motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironsmith is a smith who works iron, a skilled craftsman of the forge.

clue.text: A contemptible person on a hill, one causing trouble

blocks.note: taken as written
git is British slang for a contemptible person
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A nasty character stands on a hilltop stirring things up.
explanation.walkthrough: A + GIT + A + TOR; in a down clue 'on' simply places the first part above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up unrest, typically for a political cause, so is someone who makes trouble.

clue.text: C-in-C’s orders one’s studied at first in car

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken
being in something means enclosed by it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: in biological classification, genera and orders are both ranks
one's is 'I is', with I as the Roman numeral one
its opening letter
a limo is a limousine

explanation.surface: The commander-in-chief's instructions are read over first while riding in his car.
explanation.walkthrough: GENERA + LIMO holding IS and S. 'Orders' looks like commands, but it is the taxonomic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A generalissimo is the supreme commander of combined forces, the commander-in-chief abbreviated C-in-C.

clue.text: New shrine ultimately south of a European river

indicators.note: a new form of something is a remade one, so the letters come out rearranged
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
its final letter

explanation.surface: A newly built shrine lies at last to the south of a major river in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: SHRINE rearranged, then H. 'South' wants to be S, but 'ultimately' takes its last letter instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish is the adjective for the Rhine, meaning belonging to or coming from that great river.

clue.text: Big fire? Deduce otherwise

blocks.note: to infer is to deduce
to decide otherwise is to conclude no, the negative

explanation.surface: Is it a huge blaze? Draw a different conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'deduce otherwise' is to infer 'no', written INFER NO.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, raging fire that is out of control.

clue.text: Alliance placing silver urn originally in shelter

indicators.note: originally means at the origin or start, so only the first letter is used
placing something in another thing puts it within it

blocks.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A partnership stores the silver and an old urn under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The lee is the side sheltered from the wind, which is why it can mean shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a union of people, groups or states joined for a common purpose, just as an alliance is.

clue.text: King Edward, possibly, digesting poem about a crawler

indicators.note: digesting food means holding it inside, so one piece is swallowed by another
about means around, so a piece goes round what follows

blocks.note: King Edward is a British potato variety, and tater is slang for potato
an ode is a lyric poem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch might consume a verse about a creepy-crawly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks royal but is a popular British potato variety, and 'possibly' marks it as one example of a spud.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadeater is a fawning flatterer, the origin of toady, so a crawler or sycophant.

clue.text: Continue to perform in part of West London

blocks.note: to act is to perform
on means continuing, as in 'carry on'

explanation.surface: Keep putting on a show in one district of West London.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse clue order: ACT then ON. Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a suburb within the London Borough of Ealing, in the west of the capital.

clue.text: Stunner posed again, given rise

indicators.note: in a down clue something given a rise is lifted, so it reads upwards

blocks.note: one who posed again for a portrait resat

explanation.surface: A beautiful model sat for another portrait and got promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' looks like a beauty but is a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a brand of electroshock weapon designed to incapacitate, literally a device that stuns.

clue.text: Enemy captures leaders of soldiers storming ditch

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so the first letter of each word is taken
to capture is to take and hold, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a foe is an enemy
the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Hostile forces seize the commanders of troops charging across a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' sounds like officers in the battle scene, but it only means the first letters of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosse is a long trench or moat, especially one dug as a fortification.

clue.text: For all players, express disapproval with note

blocks.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A critic tuts at every performer and sends them a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: TUT + TI. 'Note' suggests a letter but is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a musical direction meaning the whole ensemble plays together, rather than a soloist.

clue.text: Young farm animal initially swimming lake during trial

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so just the first letter is used
during means in the course of, so one piece falls within another

blocks.note: its opening letter
a court hearing is a trial
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A lamb takes its first swim in a lake during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: S + HEARING with L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearling is a young sheep that has been shorn once, so a yearling farm animal.

clue.text: US landowner managed revolutionary rabble to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary
its opening letter

explanation.surface: An American landowner handled a rebel mob at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN + CHE + R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher owns or runs a ranch, a large livestock farm typical of the American West.

clue.text: Foot of gigantic bird that’s legendary in the East

indicators.note: in means inside, so one piece is set within another

blocks.note: taken as written
the roc is the huge mythical bird of Arabian tales
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: The foot of a giant bird of oriental legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks like part of the bird, but it is the metrical foot of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot in poetry of one stressed syllable followed by an unstressed one.
